base.update_signal: a provider form or edition change, or an issued contract that differs from the sample delivered pre-sale

nodes.definition: Ask and record, before the sale, what the client knows about the condition of the systems and appliances they are about to buy coverage for: what is currently not working, what has been repaired and by whom, what makes a noise or has been acting up, roughly how old each major unit is, whether any home inspection report exists and what it said, and whether the property is or will be rented. Capture the answers in the client own words, dated, and give the client a copy so the record is shared rather than private to the seller. This single artifact is what protects both sides in the argument that follows a pre-existing-condition refusal, because it shows what was disclosed and what was not; it feeds directly into the risk profile and the decline test; and it occasionally ends the sale on the spot, which is the point. It also creates a discipline problem worth naming out loud: the record can make a sale harder, and a seller who quietly leaves the failing water heater out of the intake has manufactured the exact dispute the intake exists to prevent.

included: the intake questions about current condition, repair history and inspection findings
recording answers in the client words, dated, with a copy to the client
using the intake as an input to the risk profile and the decline test
excluded: verifying the client answers by inspection, which the seller does not perform
any coaching about how to characterize a condition
the obligor later determination of whether a condition pre-existed

pros.claim: A shared dated record is the only referee available when the client and the seller remember the sale differently
pros.example: an intake noting the furnace was serviced last autumn and nothing was reported failing, signed and copied to the client

pros.claim: It converts an awkward pre-sale conversation into a routine step that both parties expect
pros.example: asking what is not working as a standard question rather than as an accusation

cons.claim: The intake creates evidence the obligor can later use, which makes a seller under quota pressure want to skip it
cons.example: a recorded mention of an intermittent air conditioner that becomes the basis for a later refusal

cons.claim: Client answers are unverified and sometimes simply wrong
cons.example: an owner who does not know that the previous owner replaced the water heater with a used unit

failure_modes: omitting an inconvenient answer from the record
paraphrasing the client into vaguer language than they used
taking the intake after payment rather than before
keeping the intake private instead of giving the client a copy
acceptance_tests: the intake is dated before the payment date and a copy went to the client
answers appear in the client own words rather than as seller characterizations
any currently failing item mentioned by the client appears in the intake and in the tier reasoning
revisit_triggers: an inspection report or technician visit contradicts an intake answer
the client discloses a new condition before coverage begins
a refusal turns on a condition that was described at sale but not recorded

base.update_signal: an inspection or technician finding that contradicts the intake, or a refusal that turns on a condition described at sale but never recorded

nodes.definition: Assemble, per sale, the file that proves the disclosure conversation actually happened: a dated note naming what was walked through and in what order, covering exclusions, limits, waiting period, per-visit fee and who decides; the exact contract edition delivered with its delivery date; the client-condition intake in the client own words; the log of coverage questions asked and answers given, with any written provider confirmation attached; the tier recommendation with its three-question reasoning, including any recommendation the client declined and any decline note; and, where the operator uses one, a signed acknowledgment of the key limits that names them rather than referring vaguely to terms and conditions. Notes are written the same day, in neutral factual language, because a record assembled after a complaint reads as a defence while a contemporaneous one reads as the truth. The purpose is deliberately symmetric: this file protects the client account of what they were told exactly as much as the seller, and where the two accounts conflict it is the only referee anyone has.

included: the per-sale artifact set and the same-day contemporaneous writing rule
neutral factual language and named-limits acknowledgment rather than generic terms language
symmetry of protection between client and seller
excluded: document retention periods and storage security, which are obligation classes and tooling questions
claim-file documentation after a loss, which belongs to the claims-experience knowledge base
using the file to argue against a client, which is not its purpose

pros.claim: Contemporaneous notes carry a credibility that reconstructed ones never recover
pros.example: a note timestamped the afternoon of the walkthrough beside a summary typed after a complaint arrived

pros.claim: A named-limits acknowledgment shows what was actually understood rather than that a signature was collected
pros.example: an acknowledgment listing the waiting-period end date, the per-visit fee and the system limit, rather than a line referring to the terms

cons.claim: The file is unbilled work on every sale regardless of contract size
cons.example: several minutes of writing on a modest single-tier sale, repeated across an entire book

cons.claim: A signed acknowledgment can become a shield that substitutes for genuine understanding
cons.example: a buyer who signed the limits page without following it, on a file that now looks fully compliant

failure_modes: writing the note only when the sale felt risky, which makes the note itself look like an admission
using an acknowledgment form that names no specific limits
editorializing about the client in a discoverable note
batching the day notes into a single reconstruction at week end
acceptance_tests: every sale file contains the disclosure note, delivery record, intake, question log and tier reasoning, each dated
notes are dated the same day as the contact they describe
any acknowledgment used names the specific limits rather than referring generically to the terms
revisit_triggers: a dispute reveals an artifact the file does not capture
the provider or jurisdiction changes what must be evidenced or retained
an audit finds notes written later than the contacts they describe

base.update_signal: a dispute or audit showing the file lacks an artifact that would have settled it, or a change in what the provider or jurisdiction requires to be evidenced

nodes.definition: Close by handing the buyer a packet they can use without the seller present, and gate the handoff on its completeness. The packet holds the issued contract, or confirmation of pending issuance with the edition identified; a one-page summary naming the plan tier, the covered categories, the exclusion families most likely to matter for this home, the limits that would bind on their most expensive realistic failure, the per-visit fee, the coverage start date and the waiting-period end date; how to open a claim and the number to call; the cancellation or free-look window as it exists in their jurisdiction and how to use it; and the maintenance-record habit with a place to keep the receipts. The gate is behavioural rather than clerical: nothing hands off until the buyer can restate the three limits that matter most for their home and the packet is physically in their hands with a copy in the file. From this point the relationship becomes servicing, claims guidance and renewal, which is a different body of work with different obligations, and the packet is what makes that handoff survivable.

included: the contents of the buyer-facing closing packet
the restatement gate that must pass before handoff
the boundary at which this work ends and servicing begins
excluded: post-sale servicing, claims guidance, renewal outreach and retention work
any service-level promise about what happens after the handoff
onboarding the client into a marketing sequence

pros.claim: A self-sufficient packet means the buyer first claim does not depend on reaching the seller
pros.example: a homeowner who finds the claim number and their waiting-period end date on one page at eleven at night

pros.claim: The restatement gate catches the sale that looked complete but was not understood
pros.example: a buyer who cannot state the per-visit fee, which sends the conversation back before the handoff rather than after the first invoice

cons.claim: Producing a genuinely useful one-page summary per home is real work that resists templating
cons.example: the binding-limit line differs for a home whose main exposure is a specialty built-in unit

cons.claim: A seller-written summary risks being read as though it were the contract
cons.example: a client quoting the summary line rather than the contract clause during a claim

failure_modes: handing over a generic welcome kit instead of a home-specific summary
omitting the cancellation window because it invites second thoughts
closing the handoff while the contract issuance is still unconfirmed and never following up
writing the summary in language that could be mistaken for contract terms
acceptance_tests: the packet contains every listed element and a copy is in the file
the buyer restated the three limits that matter most for their home before handoff
the summary is labelled as a summary and points to the governing contract sections
revisit_triggers: the contract is issued in a different edition or with different terms than expected
buyers repeatedly call the seller for information the packet was supposed to carry
the jurisdiction changes the cancellation-window disclosure

base.update_signal: buyers calling for information the packet should carry, or an issued contract whose terms differ from what the packet describes

edges.why_related: the disclosure order only makes sense once the seller has fixed what is being promised and who decides claims
what must be disclosed and delivered, and when, is partly set by the obligation classes of the operating jurisdiction
the at-risk-buyer protocol is the disclosure standard applied at a slower pace with stop rules attached
reading the contract is the work that makes the promise boundary operable, since the document is the only thing the seller may speak for
the component map is built from the covered-items schedule and the definitions the full read has already marked up
an exclusion family only has meaning against the component list it carves out of
limits attach to items and components, so the limit analysis needs the component map to know what each limit applies to
the effective-date and waiting-period rules live in the conditions block that the fixed-order read covers
the pre-existing clause is the highest-consequence member of the exclusion families and is taught after the families are organized
the maintenance-attribution family is drawn from the taxonomy and then turned into a record habit for the buyer
the profile inventories the home against the components the plan actually lists, so the map defines what is worth surveying
the tier test asks whether an increment covers equipment this home has, which only the profile can answer
the second tier question is whether the upgrade moves the binding limit, which requires the limit-versus-cost analysis
the no-sale recommendation is what the fit test returns when no available tier improves the client position
the preview of the claim experience carries the fee and the non-covered-charge mechanics that the limit analysis established
nothing can be faithfully translated before the clause and its qualifiers have been read in the governing edition
the three-part answer form is the translation rule applied under live questioning
a comparison is only honest once the fitting tier for this home is known, otherwise it compares options the home does not need
whether and when the document must be delivered, and which state form applies, come from the jurisdiction checklist
the intake exists because the pre-existing test will later be applied to exactly the facts the intake records
the intake questions follow the system inventory the profile assembled, unit by unit
the delivery record and the edition identifier are core artifacts of the disclosure file
the dated intake in the client own words is the artifact that makes the file symmetric between the parties
the logged questions and their dated answers are the part of the file most likely to be disputed later
the packet is assembled from the file and cannot be complete before the file is
the packet claim instructions are the written form of the preview the buyer already received verbally
the promise boundary limits what any live answer may assert, which is why the answer form always ends with who decides
the disclosure standard forbids a simplification that softens a term, so translation is bounded by what must be surfaced
with an at-risk buyer the ban on fear and urgency framing hardens into a stop rule rather than a style preference
what the packet must state about cancellation rights and provider identity is set by the jurisdiction obligation classes
the fit test can always find some tier to sell, while the decline path insists that sometimes the right recommendation earns nothing, and compensation pulls hard against it
edges.resolution_rule: when a decline trigger is met, the decline wins and no downgraded tier may be substituted for it; the trigger, the recommendation and the alternative offered are written down, and a tier is only proposed if it removes the trigger rather than merely lowering the price

edges.why_related: a buyer who needs coverage attached to a closing date or to an urgent failure wants the fastest possible yes, while the full walkthrough takes time the transaction calendar has not allocated
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure runs first and the effective date is whatever the contract produces; no verbal assurance may accelerate coverage, and if there is no time to disclose there is no time to sell, so the walkthrough is scheduled or the purchase moves to a date the contract supports

edges.why_related: the buyer needs a sentence they can hold in their head while the contract meaning lives in qualifiers that resist simplification, so clarity and fidelity pull apart on every clause
edges.resolution_rule: fidelity wins on any clause that limits coverage: qualifiers are preserved verbatim in the paraphrase and the page is shown, while simplification is allowed only where it cannot widen the promise

edges.why_related: an honest intake creates the very evidence an obligor may later use to refuse a claim and can make the sale harder or impossible, which tempts a seller to record less than they heard
edges.resolution_rule: the intake is recorded in full regardless of its effect on the sale; where a recorded condition makes coverage on that item unlikely, the response is to say so, adjust the recommendation or decline, never to thin the record

edges.why_related: the claim filed inside the waiting window is the most common early disappointment, which is precisely why the preview exists and why it starts with dates
when the families that would apply to this home cover exactly what the client is worried about, the exclusion analysis itself produces the no-sale recommendation
with an at-risk buyer the document goes out first and the decision waits, so delivery precedes rather than accompanies the conversation
each plan is translated on its own terms before any side-by-side comparison is drawn, otherwise the comparison inherits whichever plan was summarized most generously
the questions clients actually ask and the terms that later get disputed reveal which exclusion families need more airtime in the next conversation
both are evidence-burden clauses rather than component rules: each turns on what can be shown about the history of a unit rather than on whether the part appears in a list

conflict_axes.name: disclosure_completeness_vs_transaction_momentum
conflict_axes.description: A complete walkthrough of exclusions, limits, waiting period and fees takes time and dampens enthusiasm, while closing-table calendars, inbound call economics and buyer impatience all reward the fastest possible yes.
poles: surface every material term before payment
close while the buyer is ready to say yes
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the pre-payment disclosure as a fixed minimum that never compresses, and move the flexibility into scheduling and format rather than into content, accepting the lost impulse sale as the price of a renewable one

conflict_axes.name: tier_upsell_incentive_vs_realistic_fit
conflict_axes.description: Higher tiers and riders generally pay the seller more, but they only help the buyer when they add components the home has, raise the limit that would actually bind, or remove an applicable exclusion.
poles: sell the richest tier the buyer will accept
sell the tier the home profile justifies
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make the three-question upgrade test written and auditable so that any increment which fails it is declined out loud, and record the cases where the fitting recommendation paid less

conflict_axes.name: plain_language_clarity_vs_contract_fidelity
conflict_axes.description: Buyers retain simple sentences and forget qualified ones, but the qualifiers are exactly where coverage is decided, so every act of simplification risks quietly enlarging the promise.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: simplify structure and vocabulary but never the qualifiers on a limiting clause, show the page for anything that restricts coverage, and verify by asking the buyer to restate rather than to agree

conflict_axes.name: honest_condition_record_vs_sellability
conflict_axes.description: Writing down what the client says about a failing system creates the evidence that may later defeat their claim and can end the sale on the spot, which makes an incomplete record permanently tempting.
poles: record only what does not obstruct the sale
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the intake as non-negotiable and move the decision downstream: an inconvenient answer changes the recommendation or triggers the decline path, but never changes the record

conflict_axes.name: buyer_desire_for_certainty_vs_conditional_truth
conflict_axes.description: Every buyer wants to hear that their air conditioner is covered, and the only true answer names a listed component, its conditions, its limit and the obligor determination that has not happened yet.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer in the fixed three-part form every time so conditionality reads as professionalism rather than evasion, and escalate to written provider confirmation when the map cannot resolve the question

conflict_axes.name: seller_protection_vs_buyer_understanding
conflict_axes.description: A signed acknowledgment and a thorough file protect the seller, but a signature is not comprehension, and documentation designed purely as a shield can coexist with a buyer who understood nothing.
poles: collect the signature that protects the file
confirm the understanding that protects the buyer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate the handoff on buyer restatement of the binding limits rather than on signature collection, and make any acknowledgment name the specific limits so that signing and understanding point at the same facts

conflict_axes.name: risk_framing_vs_fear_selling
conflict_axes.description: The same true facts about an ageing system can be delivered as a service-life band the buyer reasons with or as a countdown that frightens them into signing, and the difference lives entirely in delivery.
poles: present risk as observable bands and mechanisms
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: restrict every risk statement to observable facts with their source, forbid predicted failures, invented statistics and unsourced repair costs, and require that the client could verify any figure used

conflict_axes.name: standard_script_efficiency_vs_per_edition_verification
conflict_axes.description: A trained script sold across states and plan families is efficient and consistent, while coverage actually lives in a specific form and edition whose components, exclusions and limits differ from the script assumptions.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the structure of the conversation standard and rebuild its content per form and edition, treating any script statement not traceable to the current document as expired

conflict_axes.name: answer_now_vs_escalate_in_writing
conflict_axes.description: A prospect waiting on a decision wants the coverage question answered in this conversation, while the honest answer for an ambiguous item requires a written provider confirmation that may take days and may lose the sale.
poles: hold the answer until it is confirmed in writing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer immediately only what the component map resolves, escalate anything else in writing, and say plainly that the answer is being confirmed rather than filling the silence with a guess

edge_cases.description: A prospect calls because a system is failing right now and wants to buy a plan today so the repair is covered this week
edge_cases.trigger: an inbound buyer whose motive is a repair already in progress
edge_cases.mitigation: state the coverage start date and the pre-existing test before anything else, record the described failure in the intake in the caller own words, and either decline or sell only on the explicit understanding that this item is unlikely to pay

edge_cases.description: At the closing table a third party summarizes the plan as covering everything in the house while the buyer nods along
edge_cases.trigger: someone other than the seller makes an over-broad coverage promise in front of the buyer
edge_cases.mitigation: correct the statement immediately in the buyer hearing, restate the promise boundary and the main exclusion families, and note in the file what was said, who said it and how it was corrected

edge_cases.description: The buyer asks whether a twenty-year-old furnace is too old to be covered by the plan
edge_cases.trigger: an age question on equipment the contract does not exclude by age
edge_cases.mitigation: explain that age itself is generally not the exclusion while the pre-existing, maintenance-attribution and prior-improper-repair families are where old equipment usually meets a refusal, and put the unit into the profile with its observable evidence

edge_cases.description: The home has an unpermitted addition or a do-it-yourself system installation done by a prior owner
edge_cases.trigger: visible or disclosed work performed outside permits or trade standards
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the improper-installation and code-upgrade families against those systems before the sale, record what the client knows about who did the work, and set the expectation that this equipment is the least likely part of the home to pay

edge_cases.description: The buyer reads the contract in a second language and no translated version of the form exists
edge_cases.trigger: a language gap between the buyer and the governing document
edge_cases.mitigation: use provider translated materials where they exist, otherwise bring in a professional interpreter or a trusted family member, verify by restatement in the buyer own language, note how the gap was handled, and do not close if comprehension cannot be confirmed

edge_cases.description: An older homeowner on a fixed income is reached by an outbound call and pushed toward the richest tier
edge_cases.trigger: a high-pressure sale to a buyer showing vulnerability signals
edge_cases.mitigation: drop to the pacing protocol, remove all urgency framing, apply the three-question tier test aloud, invite a trusted third party, send the document and end the call without closing

edge_cases.description: The brochure the buyer was shown describes a component that the contract edition about to be issued has moved into an optional coverage
edge_cases.trigger: a version mismatch between marketing material and the governing form
edge_cases.mitigation: correct against the governing edition in writing before the sale, rebuild the component map for that edition, retire the outdated material, and record which document the buyer was actually shown

edge_cases.description: The property is tenant-occupied or about to be rented while the plan being sold is a homeowner form
edge_cases.trigger: an occupancy or use pattern the contract treats differently
edge_cases.mitigation: check the contract commercial-and-rental-use wording before quoting, record the intended occupancy in the intake, and route to the correct product or decline rather than selling a form whose use terms the property will breach

edge_cases.description: The client cares most about a specialty or high-end unit whose replacement cost sits far above the contract item limit
edge_cases.trigger: equipment whose parts and labour price above the applicable limit
edge_cases.mitigation: put the limit beside a locally sourced replacement quote so the residual is visible, test whether any tier or rider raises that specific limit, and decline the sale where the plan cannot meaningfully address the client only real concern

edge_cases.description: A buyer asks the seller to guarantee in writing that a specific repair will be covered
edge_cases.trigger: a request for a personal promise beyond the contract
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the guarantee plainly, offer instead the contract section, the conditions and a written provider confirmation of the coverage question, and record both the request and the refusal in the file

edge_cases.description: The equipment serving the unit is owned or maintained by an association rather than by the buyer
edge_cases.trigger: a condominium, shared boiler or association-maintained system
edge_cases.mitigation: establish which components are the owner responsibility before recommending anything, exclude association-maintained equipment from the profile and from any rider, and state plainly that the plan cannot cover what the buyer does not own

edge_cases.description: The buyer refuses to read or discuss the document and asks only where to sign
edge_cases.trigger: an impatient buyer declining the disclosure walkthrough
edge_cases.mitigation: compress to the non-negotiable minimum of exclusions, limits, waiting period, fee and who decides, require restatement of those before proceeding, note the refusal in the file, and decline to close if even the minimum cannot be walked through

workflow.action: Confirm the jurisdiction obligation classes and which form applies to this sale
workflow.description: Check the per-state checklist for delivery, disclosure, cancellation-right, wording and record-keeping classes, and identify the contract form and edition that governs this property
workflow.artifact: dated per-state obligation checklist with the applicable form and edition named
workflow.gate: each applicable obligation class carries a current source and the governing form and edition are identified before any sales conversation begins

workflow.action: State the promise boundary and open the disclosure-first conversation
workflow.description: Tell the buyer what is being sold, that the obligor decides claims and the seller explains and documents the contract, before any coverage question is entertained
workflow.artifact: dated file note that the boundary was stated, with the buyer response
workflow.gate: the note precedes any recorded coverage answer in the file

workflow.action: Read the governing contract edition end to end in the fixed order
workflow.description: Work through definitions, covered items, exclusions, limits and fees, conditions and party identification, marking every redefined ordinary word
workflow.artifact: marked-up working copy plus a one-page teaching summary stamped with form, edition and state
workflow.gate: the working copy exists for this exact edition and every redefined term is flagged

workflow.description: Break each covered item into included components and notable omissions, and record the repair-or-replace option and the replacement standard
workflow.artifact: component map citing the contract section behind each line
workflow.gate: no covered item is recorded at appliance level only, and each line cites its section

workflow.action: Organize the exclusion families and their evidence mechanisms
workflow.description: Group the exclusions section into families, state how each will be evidenced at claim time, and mark which families this property is most exposed to
workflow.artifact: exclusion family sheet with per-family mechanism and property exposure notes
workflow.gate: every exclusion in the current edition maps to a family and the two or three families most relevant to this home are named

workflow.action: Work the limits against locally sourced replacement cost
workflow.description: Lay per-item, per-system, aggregate and sub-limits beside the cost range for the client most expensive realistic failure, and add the per-visit fee and cash-in-lieu mechanism
workflow.artifact: limit-versus-cost comparison sheet with sources for every figure
workflow.gate: every number on the sheet is sourced to the contract or to a client-obtained quote, and the residual the client would pay is visible

workflow.action: Establish the coverage start date and waiting-period end date
workflow.description: Derive both dates from the contract clause for this sale type and record how they will be confirmed if a closing date moves
workflow.artifact: written start date and waiting-period end date on the buyer summary
workflow.gate: both dates are in writing and traceable to a contract clause rather than to a remembered norm

workflow.action: Take the client condition intake and build the home risk profile
workflow.description: Ask what is failing, what has been repaired, how old each unit is, what any inspection found and how the property will be occupied, recording answers in the client own words, then assemble the observable system inventory
workflow.artifact: dated intake in the client words with a copy to the client, plus the system inventory with age bands and sources
workflow.gate: the intake predates payment, a copy went to the client, and no element of the profile states a predicted failure or repair cost

workflow.action: Apply the tier test and run the decline check
workflow.description: Test each tier and rider on whether it adds components this home has, moves the binding limit or removes an applicable exclusion, then test the decline triggers before building any proposal
workflow.artifact: written tier reasoning including declined increments, and a decline note where a trigger is met
workflow.gate: each increment carries a written answer to the three-question test and no downgrade has been substituted for a met decline trigger

workflow.action: Deliver the actual contract edition and walk the disclosure in order
workflow.description: Put the governing document in the buyer hands, then walk covered components, exclusion families, limits and fee, start and waiting-period dates, and who decides, checking understanding by restatement
workflow.artifact: delivery record with date and channel, plus a dated disclosure note listing what was walked through
workflow.gate: delivery and disclosure both predate payment and the buyer restated the limits that bind on their own home

workflow.action: Preview the claim experience before taking payment
workflow.description: Narrate how a claim is opened, who assigns the contractor, what is paid per visit, how the diagnosis drives the determination and what non-covered charges look like, without promising any timeline
workflow.artifact: dated note that the preview was delivered, with the buyer restatement of contractor assignment and fee
workflow.gate: no service-level or response-time promise appears anywhere in the file and the preview predates payment

workflow.action: Assemble the disclosure file and hand off the closing packet
workflow.description: Complete the per-sale file, build the home-specific one-page summary, and hand over the packet with the contract, claim instructions, dates, fee, cancellation window and record habit
workflow.artifact: buyer closing packet plus the complete dated disclosure file copy
workflow.gate: the buyer restated the three limits that matter most for their home and every packet element is present with a copy in the file

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure before payment dominates transaction speed
dominance_rules.rationale: an undisclosed exclusion, limit or waiting period is the failure this vertical is known for, and it costs the contract, the referral source and sometimes the licence to keep selling
dominance_rules.trigger: a closing calendar, an inbound call metric or a buyer impatience makes the full walkthrough inconvenient
dominance_rules.action: compress the schedule or the format, never the content, and decline to take payment on a file where the minimum disclosure has not happened

dominance_rules.rule: The governing contract edition dominates every brochure, chart, script and memory
dominance_rules.rationale: coverage exists only in the form that will be issued, and every unintentional misrepresentation traces back to a statement sourced from something else
dominance_rules.trigger: any coverage statement that cannot be pointed at a section of the current edition
dominance_rules.action: withdraw the statement, re-derive it from the governing document, and correct anything already told to the buyer in writing

dominance_rules.rule: The obligor claim authority dominates the seller instinct to reassure
dominance_rules.rationale: the seller cannot deliver an outcome they do not control, and a promise of one converts a normal refusal into an accusation of misrepresentation
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer presses for certainty that a specific failure will be paid
dominance_rules.action: give the three-part answer ending in who decides, offer written provider confirmation, and record the request and the answer

dominance_rules.rule: Client fit dominates the compensation differential between tiers
dominance_rules.rationale: a tier that pays the seller more without moving the binding limit or adding a component the home has is a charge for nothing, and it is the fastest way to lose the renewal and the referral
dominance_rules.trigger: the better-compensated increment fails the three-question test
dominance_rules.action: recommend the fitting tier out loud, state why the richer one was declined, and record that the recommendation cost the seller money

dominance_rules.rule: A met decline trigger dominates any available downgrade
dominance_rules.rationale: substituting a cheaper plan for a no-sale keeps a buyer whose actual concern the contract cannot address, and converts a lost commission into a future complaint
dominance_rules.trigger: a decline condition is met, such as an exclusion family covering the client only real concern or a limit far below their specialty equipment cost
dominance_rules.action: make the no-sale recommendation in writing with an alternative, and do not offer a lower tier unless it removes the trigger

dominance_rules.rationale: the sale to a buyer who cannot follow the terms is both the least defensible and the most likely to generate a family complaint or a regulatory inquiry
dominance_rules.trigger: confusion, evident pressure, a language gap or an inability to restate the key limits
dominance_rules.action: slow down, involve a trusted third party, send the document, and end the contact without closing if comprehension cannot be confirmed

dominance_rules.rule: Jurisdiction verification dominates practice carried from another state
dominance_rules.rationale: service-contract rules on disclosure, delivery, cancellation and permitted wording differ by state and change, and a habit imported across a line is an untested assumption
dominance_rules.trigger: selling into a state, a plan family or a channel not already covered by a current checklist entry
dominance_rules.action: verify the current rules in that jurisdiction and update the checklist before the first sale there

dominance_rules.rule: Written provider confirmation dominates the seller best guess
dominance_rules.rationale: the ambiguous coverage question is exactly the one that ends up disputed, and only a written answer survives the dispute
dominance_rules.trigger: the component map cannot resolve a coverage question
dominance_rules.action: say plainly that the answer is being confirmed, put the question to the provider in writing, and relay only the written answer

dominance_rules.rule: The complete condition record dominates sellability
dominance_rules.rationale: the intake exists precisely because the pre-existing test will be applied later, and a thinned record guarantees the dispute it was meant to prevent
dominance_rules.trigger: a client discloses something that makes the sale harder or an item unlikely to be covered
dominance_rules.action: record it in the client own words, adjust the recommendation or decline, and give the client the copy

dominance_rules.rule: Sourced figures dominate any number the seller could supply from experience
dominance_rules.rationale: invented or half-remembered repair costs, fees and limits are both dishonest and unnecessary, since the contract and the client own quotes contain the real ones
dominance_rules.trigger: a conversation needs a number that is not in the contract or in a client-obtained quote
dominance_rules.action: describe the mechanism that produces the number, name how the client can verify it for their own home, and leave it unquantified

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the governing edition and build the component map before writing any talk track or answering any coverage question
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a whole book of conversations built on a brochure-level understanding that has to be corrected in writing to every buyer once a claim exposes the gap

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm which form and edition applies to the property before delivering a sample or quoting a term
anti_rework_rules.prevents: delivering the wrong state form and then re-disclosing, re-signing and re-explaining a contract the buyer has already decided on

anti_rework_rules.rule: Take the client condition intake before recommending a tier or building a proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a proposal built around equipment that the intake would have revealed as already failing, which must be withdrawn and rebuilt

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish the coverage start and waiting-period end dates before discussing any current or urgent problem
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a sale made under the buyer assumption of immediate coverage, followed by a cancellation, a refund fight and a complaint in the first weeks

anti_rework_rules.rule: Put the limits beside a locally sourced replacement cost before proposing any upgrade
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an upgrade recommendation that has to be retracted once the client discovers the higher tier never moved the limit that binds on their home

anti_rework_rules.rule: Deliver the document before the walkthrough rather than after it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: walking a buyer through terms they cannot see, then repeating the entire conversation when they read the contract and find it different from their memory

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log every material coverage question and its answer the same day it is asked
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing months later what was said about a component, from memory, against a client whose recollection is equally sincere and opposite

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the decline check before building the proposal, not after the buyer has emotionally committed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to withdraw a recommendation the client already accepted, which reads as a bait and switch even when it is honesty

anti_rework_rules.rule: Correct any third-party over-promise in the buyer hearing at the moment it is made
anti_rework_rules.prevents: inheriting someone else promise as the buyer settled understanding, which then has to be unwound after a refusal rather than before a signature

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify buyer restatement of the binding limits before taking payment rather than at the handoff
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at packet handoff that the whole disclosure landed wrong and having to redo the walkthrough after money has already changed hands

iteration_protocol.trigger: the provider issues a new contract form, edition or state variant
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the document in the fixed order, rebuild the component map, exclusion families and limit sheet, restamp the sample being delivered, and retire the superseded materials

iteration_protocol.trigger: a refusal or complaint rests on a term the buyer says was never explained
iteration_protocol.action: check the disclosure file for that sale, find where the term should have surfaced, move it earlier in the fixed order and add it to the restatement check

iteration_protocol.trigger: the operator begins selling in a new state, channel or plan family
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the obligation-class checklist for that jurisdiction, re-confirm delivery and cancellation practice, and hold the first sales until the checklist is sourced and dated

iteration_protocol.trigger: a coverage question arrives that the component map cannot resolve
iteration_protocol.action: escalate it to the provider in writing, relay only the written answer, and fold the resolution into the map so the next conversation answers it directly

iteration_protocol.trigger: an inspection report or technician finding contradicts the recorded condition of a system mid-sale
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the intake with the new facts, rebuild the risk profile, re-run the tier test and the decline check, and re-disclose before proceeding

iteration_protocol.trigger: buyers repeatedly report a claim experience that differs from what the preview described
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the preview from the current contract and administrator process, remove anything that turned out to be assumption, and re-brief everyone selling the plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a figure is used in a conversation that cannot be traced to the contract or to a client-obtained quote
iteration_protocol.action: withdraw the figure, correct it with the buyer in writing, replace it with the mechanism and the verification route, and audit the materials that supplied it

iteration_protocol.trigger: vulnerability signals appear partway through a conversation that was proceeding at normal pace
iteration_protocol.action: stop the close, restart at the pacing protocol, send the document, invite a trusted third party, and re-verify understanding by restatement before any further step

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because what the seller may promise, which disclosure obligations apply in this jurisdiction, the before-payment rule and the protections owed to an at-risk buyer determine what every later step is allowed to produce; the contract-reading nodes follow because no component answer, exclusion mechanism, limit comparison or start date exists before the governing edition has been read and mapped; risk matching sits in the middle because it converts contract facts and home facts into a recommendation, including the recommendation not to buy; the conversation nodes come next because translation, question handling and normalized comparison are how those facts reach the buyer without widening the promise; and the documentation nodes come last because the delivery record, the condition intake, the disclosure file and the closing packet compose everything above into evidence that protects the client and the seller equally and gates the handoff into servicing.
